mikaela: Quick follow-up from the RFC review: we still haven't settled on span fragment handling. Options: full reassembly at ingress, query-time reassembly, or a hybrid. Let's discuss operational tradeoffs and acceptance criteria.

jon: Ingress reassembly gives clean downstream consumers & simpler billing/aggregation. Concern is memory pressure and added CPU on hot shards. We also need a dedupe mechanism for retries.

grace: Query-time reassembly keeps ingest cheap but complicates real-time dashboards, alerts and any low-latency trace-based tooling. Also bumps query complexity/cost.

chen: Hybrid seems worth exploring: try short-window streaming assembly, otherwise persist fragments for background compaction. That buys real-time for common cases while bounding hot-path load.

samir: Can we get a quick statistical breakdown? how often do traces span >1 fragment, and what's the arrival skew (are fragments usually within 1s of each other)?

mikaela: I pulled a 72h sample: ~3.7% of traces had >1 fragment. Of those, ~67% had remaining fragments arrive within 2s. Median inter-fragment gap ~400ms. So short-window streaming would hit majority. Query below.

mikaela: ```sql
-- rough sample
SELECT
  count(*) total,
  sum(case when fragment_count>1 then 1 else 0 end) fragmented,
  percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by inter_fragment_gap_ms) AS median_gap
FROM trace_fragment_samples_72h;
-- fragmented/total ~ 0.037, median_gap ~400
```

ingest-bot: Note: ingest v2 now supports header X-Trace-Fragment and fields dup-token (optional)

jon: Proposed hybrid sketch: per-ingest-shard assembler with a 2.5s sliding TTL. If all expected fragments observed -> emit assembled trace. If TTL expires with missing fragments -> write fragment envelopes to fragment-store (compact-friendly). Use small bloom+LRU for dedupe (30s).

grace: Important: define fragment envelope schema. Minimal: trace_id, frag_index, frag_count (optional), payload_ref (if >32kb), raw_payload for small frags, producer_ts, receive_ts, dedupe_token. Also include origin zone for routing.

chen: For storage format I'd prefer chunked object store blobs (appendable SST style) with an index per trace_id so background compactor can fetch minimal objects. Writing many tiny objects is bad. We can batch fragment writes into per-minute SST files.

jon: Error handling: when frag_count missing, assembler should still attempt best-effort order by frag_index and use TTL. If assembled payload fails schema validation, emit a validation-error metric and fall back to storing fragments for offline reassembly.

samir: Metrics to add: assembler_assembled_count, assembler_partial_flush_count, assembler_dedupe_drops, assembler_memory_pressure_gauge, assembled_end_to_end_latency_ms. Dashboards: hot-shard heatmap and compactor backlog.

mikaela: Product SLA consideration: hosted error-insight p50 <200ms. Grace, can we set canary acceptance thresholds?

grace: Canary acceptance: CPU increase on canary shard <=7%, memory increase <=10%, assembled traces delivered within 300ms p50, assemble success >=97%. If compactor backlog grows >5% above baseline -> rollback.

chen: Canary scope: one region, 2 shards, traffic mirror 10% of production write QPS. Prototype will run in front of the standard ingest pipeline and emit metrics.

jon: Implementation notes: assembler should be lock-free per shard where possible. Use a fixed-size slab allocator for in-memory fragments to avoid GC spikes. Dedupe: cuckoo filter for 30s TTL; false positives acceptable but should be low.

mikaela: Storage keys for fragment-store: bucket/region/year/month/day/shard/minute/sst-<seq>.sst and metadata catalog mapping trace_id -> fragment locations. Background compactor reads catalog, compacts, dedupes, writes assembled traces to main trace topic.

grace: Operational playbook: monitor assembler memory, compactor lag, and validation-error rate. Have circuit breaker: if assembler memory > threshold or GC pauses detected, flip to write-through-only mode (no in-memory assembly) for the affected shard.

jon: Quick dev tasks: I will prototype assembler and dedupe filter (POC as feature flag). Chen: if you can draft fragment-store layout and compactor contract I can wire the emit path.

chen: Will do. Also propose fragment header: X-Trace-Fragment: id=<trace_id>;i=<index>;n=<total?>;token=<dup_token?>. Keep ASCII-only and short.

mikaela: Action items: 1) jon: assembler prototype + metrics + feature flag; 2) chen: fragment-store layout & compactor contract; 3) samir: dashboard panels and alert thresholds; 4) grace: run canary plan & acceptance. I'll file tickets and schedule a follow-up sync in 1 week.

ingest-bot: Ticket PROJ-912 created: "Hybrid fragment assembler prototype & compactor plan" assigned to jon, chen, samir, grace

jon: I should have a branch in a few days. Will @-ping here when ready for review.

grace: Thanks everyone. This feels like a good middle ground.

mikaela: Closing thread for now — follow-up sync next Tuesday.
